newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end up 1/8 to 1/4.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end up 1/8 to 1/4.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended 1/8 to 1/4 point higher Tuesday amid U.S. Treasury market strength as players looked toward two new issues--totaling at least $500 million each--expected to price on Wednesday.

JP Morgan Securities Inc recorded at least $75 million of orders during the one-day retail order period it held for the $528 million New York City Municipal Assistance Corporation offering it is expected to price Wednesday.
Also Wednesday, Goldman Sachs & Co is expected to price $500 million Chicago School Reform Board of Trustees unlimited tax general obligation bonds.
"Those are going to be well-received," a trader said, referring to both deals.
"They are going to be priced right," he said, adding that the bid side "is very deep."
"Even though we are only up 1/4 of a point, I mean there's pretty good appetite for bonds in here," the trader said.
Meanwhile, no word could be gleaned from Lehman Brothers on whether a $932 million Port Authority of New York and New Jersey Airport deal would arrive this week or next.
Back in Tuesday's secondary market, action was light, market sources said.

A municipal analyst said the overall market ended up 1/8 to 1/4 point. High-grade issues improved by nearly two basis points overall, with the long end exhibiting more strength. Dollar bonds closed up 1/8 to 1/4 point, he said.

In the government cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed up 18/32 at 94-26/32 to yield 7.04 percent. A solid two-year note auction and hopes for an agreement between the Clinton administration and Republican leaders on a balance budget buoyed prices, analysts said.
In debt futures, the municipal contract closed up 12/32 at 112-31/32. The June T-bond contract closed up 15/32 at 108-4/32. The MOB spread was 155 ticks.
The analyst described Tuesday's new issue pricing as "firm."

On the competitive side, Smith Barney won $300 million Florida Department of Environmental Protection Preservation 2000 revenue bonds at a true interest cost of 5.37 percent. Bonds were reoffered to investors at a top yield of 5.4 percent in 2013.

In negotiated action, Smith Barney Inc. repriced $150 million King County, Wash., general obligation bonds, cutting yields in several maturities. The top yield was lowered to 5.75 from 5.80 percent in 2011. To see the repricing, double click on nN22206946.
